name: Giant Adenofibroma of the Breast

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological Diagnostic Criteria for Giant Adenofibroma

criteria.description: Presence of biphasic tumor with both glandular epithelial and fibrous stromal components on histology
Tumor size exceeding 5 cm in greatest dimension
Well-circumscribed, solid mass with heterogeneous echotexture on breast ultrasound or mammography
No evidence of malignant transformation or atypia on histopathology

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation of biphasic tumor with size >5 cm and absence of malignancy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires excisional biopsy and histopathological examination.

searchTerms: well-defined breast mass felt on exam

pathognomonic.symptomName: Firm, mobile breast tumor on physical examination
searchTerms: breast tumor that moves on touch
solid breast mass on physical exam

common.symptomName: Breast asymmetry due to tumor size
searchTerms: uneven breast size due to tumor
one breast larger because of tumor
mild breast pain in one area

common.symptomName: Slow progressive growth of breast mass over months
searchTerms: slowly growing breast lump over months
gradual increase in breast mass size

common.symptomName: Non-fixed tumor with no skin involvement
searchTerms: breast tumor not fixed to skin
inward nipple due to breast mass
redness of skin over breast tumor
slightly enlarged lymph nodes under arm

occasional.symptomName: Occasional breast discharge unrelated to menstruation
searchTerms: breast nipple discharge not related to period

rare.symptomName: Associated systemic constitutional symptoms (fever, weight loss)
searchTerms: fever and weight loss with tumor
systemic symptoms like fatigue and weight loss

laboratory: Routine blood tests usually normal; no specific tumor markers identified
imaging: Ultrasound showing well-circumscribed, heterogeneous solid mass
Mammography revealing large, round or oval mass with smooth margins
MRI may show well-defined lesion with mixed signal intensity
other: Histopathology demonstrating biphasic epithelial and stromal proliferation without atypia

distinguishingFeatures: Phyllodes tumors often show leaf-like stromal projections on histology
May have rapid growth and potential for malignancy
More cellular stroma with increased mitotic activity

redFlags: Rapid increase in tumor size over weeks
Skin ulceration or fixation to underlying tissues
